label: copy phase: outputting q/a/w/b/y/0, or about to output q/a
explanation: Almost entirely a copy-phase feature (98.6% of mass at t > L; nearly silent on original inputs and the <DEL> step). Within the copy phase it prefers steps whose output token is in a graded set: q (82% fire rate) > a (72%) > w, b, y (about 50%) > 0 (43%) > c, l, e, g (20-30%). It also fires one step ahead of an upcoming q or a, so activation ramps up toward a q in the copy and peaks on the step that outputs q. The top examples are sequences like 2 g s q q, where the step outputting the first q reaches the max. Fire rate is also highest at recall positions 2-4 and lower at recall position 1 and the late positions. The predicate (copy phase, output in {q,a,w,b,y,0} or next output in {q,a}) gets F1 of about 0.68 and mass recall of about 0.77 on dev. Misses are weak, diffuse activations at other copy steps; false positives are steps outputting the listed tokens that stay silent, often late in short sequences. It does not respond to the input token or to the original-phase content apart from these output identities.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output (most: q, a, w, b, y, 0; least: x, i, r, h) and the next token to output (most: q, a, w, b, y, v; least: x, i, r, h); timing cues that raise it most: t=3, phase=2, recall_idx=3.
